title: Least Loss of Passive Phase Shifters
description: LaTeX source, numerical checks (444) and a Lean 4 certificate (95 theorems) of the finite and algebraic parts of the paper Least Loss of Passive Phase Shifters. The paper proves that a passive causal system without zeros in the upper half-plane cannot shift every frequency of a band [a,b] by the same phase theta > 0 without loss: its mean attenuation over the band is at least theta (K(kappa) - E(kappa))/kappa nepers, kappa = (b-a)/(b+a), and an explicit system has the least attenuation at every frequency of the band at once. With zeros allowed, one explicit system with a single zero has the least attenuation at every frequency at once; for a right angle its mean attenuation is (pi/2)(sqrt b - sqrt a)/(sqrt b + sqrt a) nepers. With a delay added to the phase, the least mean loss without zeros is found in closed form and stays above a positive floor; with zeros the optimal system exists, is unique, has no zeros inside the band and is the limit of explicit passive polynomials solving finite convex problems, and its loss falls exponentially with the delay, at a rate between ((a+b)/pi) log cot(pi(b-a)/(4(a+b))) and pi ab/(b-a); an explicit six-tap device on an octave loses less than 7e-4 nepers.
